prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Green Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core purpose
- Tackle the cost-of-living and climate emergencies together by investing in public services, clean energy, warm homes and nature, ensuring a fair transition that lifts everyone.

Health and care
- Restore a fully public NHS; reduce waiting lists; rapid GP access; universal NHS dentistry; major mental health expansion; National Cancer Plan; support assisted dying.
- Funding: +£8bn in year one for NHS England, rising to £28bn by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years.
- Social care: free personal care for older and disabled people; better pay/careers for staff; £20bn/year. Disability benefits +5%; strengthen support for unpaid carers and children’s social care (+£3bn).

Homes and communities
- Build 150,000 new social homes per year; end Right to Buy; rent controls; end no‑fault evictions; tenant rights to energy upgrades.
- Retrofit plan: insulate homes to EPC B, heat-pump rollout, and climate adaptation (multi‑year £29bn insulation, £9bn heating, £7bn adaptation; public buildings upgrades).
- New builds to Passivhaus‑level standards; solar/low‑carbon heating mandatory; protect green space; empowered local planning.

Clean energy and climate
- No new oil and gas; cancel recent licences; end subsidies; introduce a rising carbon tax.
- Clean power push: wind to ~70% of electricity by 2030; end onshore wind barriers; 80GW offshore, 53GW onshore wind and 100GW solar by 2035; expand grid, storage and interconnectors; community ownership minimums.
- Stop new nuclear and phase out existing plants; tighten bioenergy rules.

Economy, tax and ownership
- Green investment averaging £40bn/year (rail electrification, buildings retrofit, industry decarbonisation, water/sewage, active travel).
- Bring rail, water and Big 5 energy retailers into public ownership; regional mutual banks for SMEs.
- Fair tax: wealth tax (1% >£10m; 2% >£1bn), align capital gains and investment income with earnings, NI reform, fairer inheritance tax, higher windfall taxes. Carbon tax starts at £120/t, rising toward £500/t within a decade.
- Estimated revenues: £50–£70bn/year from personal tax reforms, up to ~£80bn/year from carbon tax by end of parliament; borrow to invest, with inflation as the fiscal constraint.

Work and welfare
- £15/hour minimum wage for all; repeal anti‑union laws; day‑one rights; progress toward a four‑day week.
- Social security: +£40/week to Universal Credit; end five‑week wait, two‑child cap and sanctions; UBI as long‑term goal; protect pensions; raise Carer’s Allowance.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature Act; Clean Air Act; protect 30% of land and seas by 2030; nationalise water; Right to Roam; restore rivers/peat/woodland.
- End blood sports; curb factory farming; strong marine protections.
- Triple farm support to drive nature‑friendly farming, cut pesticides, expand horticulture and local food; free school meals for all and breakfast clubs to Year 6.

Education
- +£8bn for schools; fix unsafe buildings; £5bn for SEND; counsellors in every school; end high‑stakes testing and Ofsted; restore Sure Start; 35 hours/week childcare from 9 months.
- Abolish tuition fees; restore maintenance grants and EMA.

Transport
- Public transport subsidies to £10bn/year; free buses for under‑18s; rail renationalisation; oppose new road‑building; road‑pricing; EV scrappage and charging rollout; £2.5bn/year for walking/cycling; 20mph default in built‑up areas; frequent‑flyer levy; ban short domestic flights where trains <3 hours; no airport expansion.

Democracy, rights and migration
- Proportional representation; scrap voter ID; elected second chamber; votes at 16; stronger lobbying/media transparency.
- Defend Human Rights Act; support trans self‑ID.
- End hostile environment; safe asylum routes; right to work; simplify visas; NHS access for migrants; remove spousal income rules.

Justice and drugs
- Rebuild trust in policing; end routine stop‑and‑search and facial recognition; misogyny as a hate crime; £11bn to restore courts/legal aid; presumption against short prison terms; decriminalise personal drug possession with health‑led support.

Foreign policy
- Uphold international law; support Ukraine; push immediate Gaza ceasefire, recognise Palestine, end UK arms exports to Israel, pursue war‑crimes accountability.
- Restore aid to 0.7% GNI and rise to 1% by 2033; climate finance to 1.5% GNI incl. Loss and Damage.
- Path to rejoin the EU via Customs Union, free movement and Erasmus; sign the UN nuclear‑ban treaty; reform NATO with no‑first‑use.
